newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen closes Orimulsion power station.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen closes Orimulsion power station.

text.p: PowerGen Plc, Britian's second biggest power generator, said on Wednesday it was closing its 500 megawatt Ince power station and would not renew a five-year contract for Orimulsion, dubbed the world's filthiest fuel.
PowerGen said it would try to redeploy the 41 staff employed at Ince or seek voluntary redundancies.

"The Ince closure will follow the ending of the five-year Orimulsion contract for Ince which will not be renewed," PowerGen said in a statement. The company said the Ince power station, near Chester in north west England, would stop generating electricity at the end of next March.

To make up for the loss of power, PowerGen will bring back into operation a generating unit at Fiddler's Ferry power station in Warrington, also north west England. The unit was placed in reserve in March 1994 and should return to commercial operating in December.

The closure of Ince marks the end of PowerGen's current dealings with Orimulsion, a cheap fuel from Venezuela that has triggered attacks from environmentalists and legal action from a car firm that alleged fallout damaged paintwork on new cars.
PoweGen in March closed its Richborough power plant in Kent -- the only other of its three originally oil-fired power stations that had been adapted to burn Orimulsion.

The company's other power station, on the Isle of Grain in Kent, burns mainly oil. PowerGen does not plan to invest the necessary capital or fit a new special filter to convert it for Orimulsion use, a company spokesman said.
